newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ROW FLARES OVER UEFA BACKING FOR GERMAN WORLD CUP BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROW FLARES OVER UEFA BACKING FOR GERMAN WORLD CUP BID.

text.p: A row flared up on Saturday over UEFA's stated backing of Germany's bid to stage the 2006 World Cup finals, brushing aside English hopes.

At a hastily called news conference, English F.A. spokesman David Davies said they had received a fax on Friday in which UEFA said its executive committee "recalled that it had already committed itself to supporting the candidature of Germany as organiser of the World Cup in 2006."
Davies told reporters: "It made no reference as to when or where this decision had been taken. At this stage there is no evidence that it was ever recorded publicly."

He added: "UEFA has informed us that the (executive) committee had also confirmed its belief that there should only be one candidate from each continental confederation when bids were submitted to stage the tournament."
Davies stressed: "The final decision as to who stages the World Cup of 2006 is scheduled to be taken in June of the year 2000 by FIFA, football's world governing body. It is not a decision for UEFA."
He said the F.A. had no alternative but to see the fax as "evidence of an attempt at a very early stage to prevent England's bid from receiving proper consideration."
Davies warned: "The attempt will not succeed."
F.A. chief executive Graham Kelly said: "We cannot sit back and allow this sort of thing to happen to English football. We have a duty to the game in England."
He added: "It's not a dispute between England and Germany. We have stressed that we want both bids to be considered fairly, openly and democratically."
The F.A. were in talks with UEFA until late on Friday. Kelly described the situation as "entirely unacceptable."
After successfully staging Euro 96 last year, English officials feel their World Cup claims for 2006 are particularly strong.
